data.description: Contains a Saint's Relic to provide area healing that increases in effectiveness for each Age. Cannot be moved to other Landmarks or buildings with defenses.

data.name: Archery Range
data.description: Produces ranged infantry units.

data.name: Barracks
data.description: Produces melee infantry units.

data.name: Blacksmith
data.description: Houses technology to improve infantry and cavalry.

data.name: Capital Town Center
data.description:
All Resources can be dropped off here. Produces Villagers, Scouts, and increases your maximum Population. Adds additional attacks while garrisoned.
Capital Town Centers can detect units stealth or disguises.

data.name: Dhùn Èideann
data.description: Equipped with the "Seven Sisters" cannons to defend the area. Produces gunpowder siege engines for 100 less Gold. Gunpowder siege weapons gain 1 tile range.

data.name: Dock
data.description:
Produces naval units.
Automatically repairs nearby damaged naval units.
Capable of holding up to three Fishing Ships.

data.name: Farm
data.description:
Harvestable Food source. Use a Villager to gather Food from the Farm.
Only one Villager can work each Farm.

data.name: Fishpond
data.description:
Harvestable Gold source. Use a Kirkman to gather 40 Gold per minute from the Fishpond. While the Fishpond is being worked, nearby workers gather resources 20% faster.
Fishpond capacity: 1 for every Lowland Landmark built to a total of 4.

data.name: Guardian of Scotland
data.description: Build and defend a Wonder to secure victory. Rival civilizations will be aware of its construction and seek to destroy it.

data.name: House
data.description: Increases your maximum Population.

data.name: Keep
data.description:
Heavy garrison and defensible position. Can be upgraded with weaponry. Adds additional attacks while garrisoned. 
When destroyed, Keeps become repairable Keep Ruins and sabotage the surrounding area for 60 seconds. Enemies within sabotaged area have reduced combat effectiveness. Keep Ruins can be restored if repaired at any point within 60 seconds and can be restored for up to 600 Stone, after which repairing becomes free.

data.name: Lumber Camp
data.description: Villagers can drop off Wood at this building. Houses technologies to improve Wood gathering.

data.name: Market
data.description: Allows the buying and selling of resources and produces the Trader.

data.name: Mill
data.description: Villagers can drop off Food at this building. Houses technologies to improve Food gathering.

data.name: Mining Camp
data.description: Villagers can drop off Stone and Gold at this building. Houses technologies to improve mining.

data.name: Monastery
data.description: Produces religious units and houses religious technologies. Starting in the Castle Age (III), religious units can pick up Relics and place them in this building to generate Gold.

data.name: Mustering Hall
data.description:
Holds technology from the Highlands and Lowlands. Each time a Landmark from a region is chosen, costs of their powerful technologies are reduced. Musters warriors using Food and Muster Charge costs. Each type of muster is one-time use.
Generates influence to military production buildings. Each building provides a count towards Muster Hall levels to improve its mustering efficiency and adds additional Muster Charges.
Comes with 1 Muster Charge by default.

data.name: Palisade
data.description: Light defensive wall for quickly fortifying an area.

data.name: Palisade Gate
data.description: Light defensive gate. Must be built on a Palisade Wall segment.

data.name: Siege Workshop
data.description: Produces siege engines and powerful gunpowder units.

data.name: Snowdoun Gate
data.description:
Produces toggled infantry for free with a value of 190 resources per minute. 
Technologies researched at the Mustering Hall increase infantry production speed at this Landmark by 15%. When enemies are nearby, infantry hasten their deployment and gain an additional 15% production speed.

data.name: Stable
data.description: Produces cavalry military units.

data.name: Stone of Destiny
data.description: Buildings constructed around the Stone of Destiny have 30% of their construction cost rebated as Gold. Does not apply to Landmarks. Grants early access to Kirkman that can create Fishponds.

data.name: Stone Wall
data.description:
Sturdy wall that cannot be attacked by torches. 
Units on walls take 25% less damage from ranged attacks, 50% less damage from siege attacks, and their range is increased by +1.

data.name: Stone Wall Gate
data.description:
Heavy defensive gate. Must be built on a Stone Wall segment.
Infantry can use the gate to access the top of the walls.

data.name: Stone Wall Tower
data.description:
Heavy defensive tower that fires a springald. Must be built on a Stone Wall segment.
Infantry can use the tower to access the top of the walls.

data.name: Three Loch Lookout
data.description: Has a large line of sight and adds 3 muster charges for the Mustering Hall or Three Loch Lookout. The number of warriors received from mustering is increased by 75%. Comes with the option to muster a navy if constructed adjacent to water.

data.name: Tower House
data.description: Produces Highland Cattle, has extended line of sight, and detects units in stealth or disguises. Can be upgraded with weaponry and fortifications. Attacks while garrisoned. Increases maximum population by 15.

data.name: Tower of Skye
data.description: Acts as a Tower House equipped with arrowslits and a springald emplacement. Creates a local Stealth Forest and increases infantry damage by 15% while in Stealth Forests. Tower Houses unlock the ability to create additional Stealth Forests. Galleys unlock the Fairy's Chosen ability.

data.name: Town Center
data.description:
All Resources can be dropped off here. Produces Villagers, Scouts, and increases your maximum Population. Adds additional attacks while garrisoned.
Non-Capital Town Centers can't detect stealth or disguises.

data.name: University
data.description: Houses advanced technology that benefit the civilization.
